stem:
A 60-year-old man with hypertension is prescribed an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor.

The blocked enzyme normally catalyzes which of the following conversions, and in which organ is it chiefly produced?

options.label: A
options.text: Angiotensinogen to angiotensin I, produced in the kidneys
options.misconception: Renin's reaction and source are being attributed to ACE.
options.explanation: Renin, secreted by juxtaglomerular cells of the afferent arteriole, cleaves angiotensinogen into angiotensin I; ACE performs the next step and comes from the lungs.

options.label: B
options.text: Angiotensin I to angiotensin II, produced in the lungs
options.misconception: None; pulmonary ACE activates angiotensin II.
options.explanation: Angiotensin I is not biologically active until converted to angiotensin II by angiotensin-converting enzyme from the lungs; inhibiting ACE reduces the vasoconstrictor and aldosterone drive.

options.label: C
options.text: Angiotensinogen to angiotensin I, produced in the liver
options.misconception: The substrate's origin is being confused with the enzyme that converts it.
options.explanation: The liver makes angiotensinogen, the circulating substrate; converting it to angiotensin I is renin's job, and ACE converts angiotensin I to II in the lungs.

options.label: D
options.text: Angiotensin II to angiotensin III, produced in the adrenal cortex
options.misconception: A downstream degradation step is being offered as the blocked reaction.
options.explanation: ACE activates rather than degrades: it converts inactive angiotensin I into the potent vasoconstrictor angiotensin II, and it is produced in the lungs.

options.label: E
options.text: Vasopressin to its active metabolite, produced in the hypothalamus
options.misconception: An unrelated peptide hormone is being inserted into the cascade.
options.explanation: ADH is synthesized in the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary without an activation step; ACE's substrate is angiotensin I, converted in the lungs.

context: Learning objective: map the renin-angiotensin cascade. Renin converts angiotensinogen to angiotensin I; lung-derived ACE converts angiotensin I to active angiotensin II.
imageCaption: Nephron segments: filtration, PCT, loop, DCT, collecting duct (ADH aquaporins).
